transcript.answer: No, not any more. Issue #191 changed the client rule, so busy is cleared only on `stream_end` or socket close. Originally (`044`) the client also cleared `busy` on an `error` frame. Engine change #148 (`139`) made `stream_end` the single terminal frame, sent once per accepted message. A probe had found an unrelated `INVALID_MESSAGE` error landing between two `entry_delta` frames of a healthy stream. A client that cleared `busy` on that error would drop the typing indicator and unlock the composer mid-answer. FR-013 now requires `busy` to stay true from send until `stream_end` or close. It also has a test asserting that an `error` frame alone never clears `busy`. The error frame still sets `state.error`.

judgements.reason: The answer says no, cites the INVALID_MESSAGE error arriving between entry_delta frames of a healthy stream, names stream_end as the single terminal frame sent once per accepted message, and says busy clears only on stream_end or socket close, which covers everything in the gold answer.
